sub.en: Look at the sentences. What happens to the verb after he, she and it? And where does the frequency word go?

items.q: I ___ up at six.
She ___ up at five.
items.why: he / she / it → add -s. All the other persons keep the base form.

items.q: He ___ the housework on Sunday.
My colleague ___ English every evening.
She ___ at seven o’clock.
items.why: The frequency word goes before the main verb.

items.q: He ___ late.
items.why: …but after am / is / are: he is never late.

acts.title: The day I would live again
text: Marat, 34: “My perfect day starts late. I wake up at nine, but I hardly ever get up before ten. I have a long shower, and then I do the shopping — I love a quiet supermarket on a Tuesday morning. In the afternoon I cook for four hours. I never look at my phone. In the evening my friends come and eat everything.”

Aigul, 27: “My ideal day is a work day. I get up at half past five and I always have twenty minutes with a coffee before anybody else wakes up. I start work at seven and I finish at three, so the afternoon is mine. I go swimming twice a week and I usually relax with a book after dinner.”
Bekzat, 52: “I don’t need anything special. I take the bus to the mountains, I walk for six hours and I speak to nobody. My wife thinks this is a terrible day. She sometimes comes with me anyway.”

items.s: Marat usually gets up before ten.
Aigul’s perfect day is a work day.
Bekzat’s wife loves this kind of day.

write.q: Describe your perfect day: 6 sentences from morning to night. Use at least four frequency words, and one sentence about another person with he or she.
write.model: On my perfect day I wake up at eight and I never look at my phone before breakfast. I always have a long shower and I usually walk to work. I hardly ever take the bus. I have a break at eleven and I finish work at four. My sister sometimes comes for dinner — she cooks better than I do. I go to bed early, about ten.

speak.q: Answer out loud: What time do you get up? How often do you do the shopping? What do you never do? Then describe one person’s routine with he or she.
speak.model: I usually get up at half past six. I do the shopping once a week, on Saturday. I never drink coffee after six. My brother gets up at five — he always takes the bus and he hardly ever comes home before eight.
